result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

Per the Corvid Retail Subscription Agreement (DOC-0001), a credit arises only if monthly regional uptime is below 99.5%, and 'no other credits apply'. The final SRE uptime report for March 2026 (DOC-0211) shows Corvid Retail (us-central) at 99.94%, above the 99.5% threshold - the March incident INC-2291 affected the us-west region (Beacon Health), not Corvid's region. Separately, even if the SLA had been missed, the contractual credit would be 10% x USD 11,500 = USD 1,150, not USD 2,500. Recommend billing/CS respond to the customer declining the credit; escalate to Controller if a goodwill concession is desired (that would be a commercial decision outside the SLA terms and should not be recorded as an SLA credit).

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 close: US billing adjustments (usage overages & SLA credits)
Prepared by: david.murguia@gmail.com (senior accountant) | Date: 2026-04-03 | Entity: Halvard Systems Inc. (US), period 2026-03

SCOPE
Bill usage overages due under contract and process SLA credits customers are entitled to. Every customer request was tested against the governing contract and the final March 2026 usage (DOC-0210) and uptime (DOC-0211) reports before anything was booked.

1) USAGE OVERAGES - one customer qualifies
Only Acme Logistics has contractual usage/overage terms (Order Form 3, DOC-0003: 1,000,000 API calls included per calendar month, overage USD 0.004/call, billed monthly in arrears on the Halvard usage report). The Beacon Health (DOC-0002) and Corvid Retail (DOC-0001) agreements are flat-fee subscriptions with no usage component; no contract is on file for Fairview Labs or Evergreen Bank, and neither exceeded 1,000,000 calls in any event.

  Acme Logistics: 1,284,000 calls - 1,000,000 included = 284,000 x USD 0.004 = USD 1,136.00
  Beacon Health 412,300 / Corvid Retail 688,150 / Fairview Labs 97,420 - all under 1,000,000 and/or no overage terms: nothing to bill.

  JE-00304 (2026-03-31): Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables 1,136.00 / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue 1,136.00
  Support: DOC-0003 (contract), DOC-0210 (final usage report).
  Note on classification: the March overage invoice has not yet been issued (the metering report was finalized 2026-04-01), so the amount is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables per Accounting Policy Manual sec. 6 rather than to 1100 AR. Jan and Feb overages (INV-2119 USD 612.00, INV-2120 USD 844.00) were booked directly to AR because invoices existed at the time. Billing should raise the March overage invoice to Acme and reclass 1300 -> 1100 on issuance.

2) SLA CREDITS - one customer entitled, one request declined
  Beacon Health (us-west) - ENTITLED. March uptime 99.31%, below the 99.5% threshold (incident INC-2291, 2026-03-11, 5h02m). Contract DOC-0002 provides a credit of 10% of that month's subscription fee, applied against the customer's receivable balance: 10% x USD 8,000.00 = USD 800.00.
  JE-00305 (2026-03-31): Dr 4000 Subscription Revenue 800.00 / Cr 1100 Accounts Receivable 800.00
  Support: DOC-0002 (contract), DOC-0211 (final uptime report). Recorded as a reduction of the related revenue per policy sec. 7.
  Cash note: Beacon paid INV-2112 in full on 2026-03-19 (JE-00270), so this credit creates an USD 800.00 credit balance in Beacon's AR that will be applied against the April invoice. AR/billing should be notified so the credit memo is reflected in the subledger and the April bill.

  Acme Logistics (us-east) 99.97% and Corvid Retail (us-central) 99.94% - both above 99.5%, no SLA credit due. Evergreen Bank 99.97% and Fairview Labs 99.99% likewise.

3) EXCEPTION LOGGED (EXC-001) - Corvid Retail USD 2,500 credit request: NOT BOOKED
Corvid Retail Finance requested a USD 2,500 outage credit on their next invoice (DOC-0202, 2026-03-30). No credit is contractually due and nothing was posted:
  - Corvid's March uptime was 99.94% (DOC-0211), above the 99.5% SLA threshold. The March incident (INC-2291) hit the us-west region; Corvid is in us-central and was not affected.
  - The agreement (DOC-0001) states a credit arises only on a sub-99.5% month and that "no other credits apply."
  - The requested amount is also inconsistent with the contract: the maximum contractual credit would be 10% x USD 11,500 = USD 1,150, not USD 2,500.
Recommend Billing/CS respond declining the request. Any goodwill concession would be a commercial decision outside the SLA and requires Controller approval; it should be recorded as a discount/concession, not as an SLA credit.

NET P&L IMPACT (US, March 2026): +USD 1,136.00 usage revenue (4100), -USD 800.00 subscription revenue (4000) = net +USD 336.00.

APPROVALS / CONTROLS
Both entries are below the USD 10,000 senior-accountant posting limit (policy sec. 1), so no Controller approval request was required; no transaction was split to stay under the threshold. Both entries carry their supporting documents (policy sec. 2). No entry was posted to force a reconciliation.

CHECKLIST
US "Revenue recognition" set to in_progress - the usage-overage and SLA-credit adjustments in scope here are complete, but the item remains open for the revenue accountant's remaining subscription/deferred revenue and professional services procedures.

OPEN ITEMS FOR CONTROLLER
  a. Approve the response declining Corvid Retail's USD 2,500 request (EXC-001).
  b. Confirm Billing issues the Acme March overage invoice (USD 1,136.00) and the Beacon Health USD 800.00 credit memo in April, with the 1300 -> 1100 reclass on invoicing.
  c. No master agreement is on file for Fairview Labs or Evergreen Bank. This did not affect March (neither had overage usage or an SLA miss), but the contract file should be completed so future usage and SLA terms can be tested.
